slides.title: Ember & Oak
slides.subtitle: A small roastery on our street, with a counter you can walk up to
slides.notes: Thanks for coming, and thanks for doing it here rather than in a meeting room. This is a short one: what we want to build, why the street can carry it, and what we're asking. Five slides, then questions.

slides.text: We already drink good coffee here. We just buy it roasted somewhere else.
slides.notes: Say it plainly: the neighbourhood has the taste, the foot traffic and the cafés. What it doesn't have is a place where the beans are roasted a few streets away. That's the whole gap.

slides.title: Why it works on this street

items.title: Roasted around the corner
items.body: Beans roasted this week and sold this week. No warehouse, no six-week-old bag.

items.title: A counter people pass
items.body: The school run, the dog walk, the tram stop. We are already on the way.

items.title: Local cafés and restaurants
items.body: Small weekly orders from kitchens within cycling distance, delivered by us.

slides.notes: Three reasons, and they hold each other up: freshness is only sellable if people can reach you, and the counter pays the rent while wholesale grows slowly. Keep this slide to a minute.

slides.title: From keys to first wholesale account

steps.title: Keys and a build-out
steps.body: Sign, strip the back room, order the roaster.

steps.title: Roaster in
steps.body: Machine installed, first test roasts, house blend dialled in.

steps.title: Doors open
steps.body: Counter, bags on the shelf, the neighbours who backed it in first.

steps.title: Wholesale
steps.body: First cafés and restaurants on a weekly round.

slides.notes: Be honest about the slow parts: permits and the build-out set the pace, everything after that is roasting. Five months from signature to the first wholesale invoice is the plan, not a promise.

slides.title: Let's open the doors
slides.subtitle: [€ amount] for the roaster, the build-out and the first six months of working capital. Small cheques welcome.
slides.notes: Land the ask and then stop talking. Say what the money buys, say that small amounts are genuinely useful, and invite people to come and see the space before they decide.
